body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It's Wednesday, November 4, and the morning after Election Day has left Kern County with a new governor-elect, a housing bond headed for passage, and one billionaire tax still too close to call. Closer to home, an oil spill shut down northbound Highway 99, and a head-on crash near the county line sent one person to the hospital with a serious head injury. It's 54 degrees at Meadows Field with a high near 68 ahead, no weather alerts, and air quality sitting at a healthy 35.

## The Kern Overnight

The night's most serious call came at 10:44 p.m., when officers were sent to a weapons report after a man was said to be holding a firearm. People could be heard screaming in the background, and the caller's line went down before dispatchers could gather more. Violence carried through the rest of the night: officers were sent to the 600 block of Casa Loma Drive in southeast Bakersfield at 11:39 p.m., where a man in his 30s was reported to have pushed his mother and then walked toward Brundage Lane. A fight inside a home with several people involved was reported at 5:49 a.m., and a battery at a market in the 400 block of Baker Street in east Bakersfield came in at 7:29 p.m.

Two searches ran alongside the violence. A 3-year-old boy was reported missing from a home on El Toro Drive in south Bakersfield at 7:45 p.m., last seen in a black Lightning McQueen shirt, green cargo pants and orange and red shoes. A traffic stop turned into a pursuit at 10:47 p.m. and ended with two men running off on foot, and after 1 a.m. officers chased a store burglary from Niles Street to Pacific Street, where a clerk had yelled for a man to come back as he ran to a waiting car carrying a box. One person was taken into custody in the 900 block of Pacific.

The two worst crashes arrived before daylight. A car crossed from the southbound side of Interstate 5 into oncoming traffic near the Kern-Kings county line at 3:36 a.m. and hit a white Ford pickup head-on. The vehicles came to rest about 200 yards apart; of the four people inside them, three were unhurt and one suffered a serious head injury. An air ambulance was requested and then cancelled, and a ground ambulance took the patient. At 4:52 a.m., fire crews were sent to the Norris Road on-ramp to northbound Highway 99 for a semi crash with a possible gas leak and found the rig across at least three lanes just north of the east off-ramp to Highway 58. The CHP stopped traffic while crews worked, and fire units caught in the backup reached the scene along the shoulder.

## Today's weather

Expect a high near 68 degrees today and a low around 52 tonight, with the current observation at Meadows Field reading 54. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and air quality is good at an index of 35 — a comfortable, unremarkable valley day, the kind that makes the morning commute the only real obstacle. No active fires were reported in the county as of this writing.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that an oil spill shut down northbound Highway 99, the same stretch of freeway where a semi crash had already blocked three lanes before dawn.** Details on the spill itself were limited in early reporting, but the closure added a second major headache to the northbound side of the highway in a single morning, and drivers heading toward the Highway 58 interchange should expect delays until crews clear the scene.

**According to 23ABC, it is too early to call the outcome of Proposition 40, the California measure that would impose a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of billionaires.** With almost 6 million votes still to be counted, the AP Decision Team is waiting on additional results. Opponents have outnumbered supporters across most of the state, with sizable "no" leads in the Inland and Central Valley region, San Diego and Orange County, and narrower leads along the central coast and in the Bay Area; "yes" votes led narrowly in Los Angeles County and on the northern coast. The measure divided liberal leaders nationally — Vermont Sen. Bernie Sanders framed it as a monumental step toward reining in wealth inequality, while Gov. Gavin Newsom warned it would push the state's wealthiest residents to leave and take their tax money with them. The "no" side raised roughly ten times as much as the "yes" side, largely from tech moguls and venture capitalists. Most of the revenue would be dedicated to replacing federal funding cuts to healthcare.

**23ABC also reports that Proposition 1, the state's $11.25 billion affordable housing measure, is projected to pass based on early AP results.** A "yes" vote allows California to borrow the money through bonds to build affordable housing, supporting rental and supportive housing, home loans for military veterans, and down payment assistance. Supporters argued the state needs more affordable homes and that the investment would help working families, veterans and people at risk of homelessness; opponents questioned taking on billions in new debt and said the state should focus on why housing is so expensive in the first place.

**Kern County voters weighed in on the governor's race, and 23ABC spoke with several of them about why they cast their ballots the way they did.** The Associated Press projects Democrat Xavier Becerra will be California's next governor, defeating Republican Steve Hilton. The voters 23ABC interviewed supported Becerra for personal reasons — one said he relates to her community and cares deeply about the Latino community, while another tied the decision to Kern County's oil and gas industry and the local economy. Unofficial results show Becerra leading statewide with ballots still being counted, and the voters said they will be watching closely to see how the next governor handles the issues they brought to the ballot box.

**KGET 17 reports that David Couch has collected 44,000 votes so far in an unopposed race for State Assembly.** With no challenger on the ballot, the tally reflects voters who cast a ballot in the race regardless. In another local contest, KGET 17 reports the Kern High School District Area 1 incumbent is leading with more than 50% of the vote as counting continues.

**Bakersfield Now reports on a piece of history elsewhere in the country: South Carolina has elected Democrat Annie Andrews to the U.S. Senate, defeating Darline Graham.** The result adds another data point to a midterm cycle still being sorted out across the country, and it lands the same morning Kern County is working through its own local races.

## Something good

The most positive headline this morning is that California's $11.25 billion affordable housing measure, Proposition 1, is poised to pass, according to the Associated Press. If the projection holds, the measure would direct significant state funding toward affordable housing across California — rental and supportive housing, veterans' home loans, and down payment help for families trying to buy their first home. For a valley where housing costs have climbed faster than wages for years, that is real money aimed at a real problem.

## Coming up this week

Election results will keep updating through the week as county elections officials work through the remaining ballots, so expect the numbers in the local races to shift before anything is final. On the government side, the Police Civil Service Commission meets today, November 4, at 8:30 a.m., and the Bakersfield City Council has two sessions on the calendar today — a 3:30 p.m. meeting and a 5:15 p.m. meeting. The Planning Commission meets Thursday, November 5, at 5:30 p.m., which is the one to watch if you have thoughts about a development proposal near you.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a full slate. Journey USA takes the stage Saturday, November 7, and Texas Tornado Tradition follows the same day. The 2026 Golden Empire Youth Cheer Expo fills the Fox on Sunday, November 8, and the Cults & Classics series screens "Play Misty for Me" on Monday, November 9. The Nutcracker! Magical Christmas Ballet arrives November 13, and season passes for the 2026–2027 Cults & Classics series are already on sale. Have a good Wednesday, and drive carefully out there — the northbound 99 is not where you want to be this morning.

top.title: Oil spill shuts down northbound Hwy 99
